thread:
maria: FYI during the canary this morning one GPU shard slipped into a slower decode loop and the continuous batcher kept aggregating for it. result: other tenants got pulled into a long tail. we need safe fallbacks.
kevin: saw it. traces show the batcher waited ~25ms repeatedly for the slow slot and queued more requests. big amplification.
anjali: do we currently expose shard health to the admission layer? iirc we only surface per-host metrics, not shard-level hints.
sam: short-term fix idea: per-shard fallback modes: NORMAL (pack aggressively) -> CONSERVATIVE (looser packing) -> MICRO_WINDOW (fixed small batches / bypass packing). transitions triggered by consecutive p90 violations or explicit health flag.
maria: sounds promising. micro-window avoids blocking others but costs more tokens for that shard. tradeoff: global latency vs per-shard unit cost. fine if it's temporary.
kevin: implement hysteresis: require N consecutive window breaches and a cooldown. also cap transitions per-minute to avoid flip-flop.
anjali: add quota shaping when in MICRO_WINDOW so the shard can't flood the scheduler. simple token-bucket decrease per-shard should work.
sam: agree. also preserve KV cache locality: when switching route, keep existing in-flight requests on the primary path for a short overlap (e.g., 150-250ms) so KV isn't thrashy. new requests go to micro-window.
maria: +1. that overlap reduces cold-decode churn. also expose a warmup hint so the other path can prefetch KV entries for hot keys.
kevin: config sketch:
```
shard_fallback:
  p90_threshold_ms: 60
  consecutive_windows: 3
  cooldown_seconds: 30
  overlap_ms: 200
  micro_window_size: 2
```
kevin: runtime override via console for canaries.
anjali: for observability, ops needs a "shard-impact" metric: per-shard p50/p90/p99 and delta_vs_cluster. ops-bot: can you create that?
ops-bot: created dashboard card + metric name: infra.shard_packing_impact, alert rule pending (will ping infra board). link: https://confluence.internal/infra/shard-packing-impact.
sam: let's also let clients tag requests with latency_sensitivity: high|normal and allow_batching: false to opt out of packing. useful for customers who pay for tight SLOs.
maria: yes. default behavior should be conservative for high-sensitivity requests. document the queue contract.
kevin: testing plan: synthetic load with mixed sizes, inject shard slowdown, assert less than 5% p99 regression on unaffected tenants and no global tail >X ms. run with 5 runs across different traffic mixes.
anjali: add a short postmortem template to capture timeline, metric delta, mitigation chosen, perf cost delta. keep it 1 pager.
maria: who owns the RFC follow-up? sam?
sam: i'll write the follow-up RFC and a minimal POC (micro-window allocator + shard-health hook). target draft by next week.
maria: actions: sam RFC, ops add metric/alerts (ops-bot done), kevin prototype config, anjali write hysteresis rules + test cases. reconvene after RFC.
kevin: one more: add a debug-only client flag to bypass packing to reproduce locally without cluster churn. very helpful during investigations.
anjali: +1. makes debugging deterministic.
ops-bot: alert rule created: shard_packing_impact > 1.5x baseline triggers #eng-runtime-alerts. email to oncall.
maria: great. thanks all.
